Honour-based abuse

42. “Honour”-based abuse is often referred to as “so called” because there is a need to be clear
that there is no honour in abuse. Whilst there is no statutory definition of honour-based
abuse, the common definition adopted across government and criminal justice agencies is
as follows:
“An incident or crime involving violence, threats of violence, intimidation, coercion or abuse
(psychological, physical, sexual, financial or emotional abuse), which has or may have
been committed to protect or defend the honour of an individual, family and/or community
for alleged or perceived breaches of the family and/or community's code of behaviour.”
